page_title_verbatim: Servicios VIP para la clase Business - Iberia España

finding_F53_AIRPORT_SERVICES_ARE_A_FARE_.claim: Iberia's airport services are bundled with Business class, not sold as add-ons. The page title scopes them to a fare class in its own words.
services_verbatim_es: trato preferente en el embarque, desembarque y en la entrega de equipaje
Acceso rápido en el control de seguridad
translation: preferential treatment at boarding, disembarking and baggage delivery
finding_F53_AIRPORT_SERVICES_ARE_A_FARE_.no_price_observed: The page carries no purchase price for any service. Searched for € figures, 'desde', 'precio', 'coste', 'tarifa' — only a generic 'Mejor precio garantizado' (best price guaranteed) appeared, which refers to fares, not services.
finding_F53_AIRPORT_SERVICES_ARE_A_FARE_.scope_limit: One airline, one page, Spanish market. American Airlines and Qatar are untouched and may sell these separately — that is exactly what tier 4 was widened to test.

finding_F54_THE_BUSINESS_GOAL_HAS_A_PROB.claim: Business goal 5 assumes airport services are a purchasable product. On the first supplier examined they are a fare-class entitlement, which changes who Luma would be selling to.
finding_F54_THE_BUSINESS_GOAL_HAS_A_PROB.the_goal_verbatim: Increase usage of airport services such as lounges and Fast Track (scenario.pdf, Business Goals)
finding_F54_THE_BUSINESS_GOAL_HAS_A_PROB.what_this_capture_implies: If lounges and Fast Track come free with Business class, then the addressable market for selling them is ECONOMY passengers — a different product entirely, and one already occupied by third-party aggregators (Priority Pass, LoungeKey, DragonPass class of product), none of which is on the roster.
finding_F54_THE_BUSINESS_GOAL_HAS_A_PROB.confidence: Verified as an observation about Iberia; the market inference is Inferred, from this single capture.
our_product_decision_required: Decision required: is Luma selling airport services to economy travellers — competing with lounge aggregators nobody has analysed — or surfacing entitlements travellers already hold and do not know about? The second is a reassurance feature and needs no inventory. The first is a business Luma has not scoped.

Decision required: Luma's stated user is a first-time traveller on a limited budget. They are not in Business class. Goal 5 and the target user may be pulling in opposite directions, and that should be settled before design.
finding_F54_THE_BUSINESS_GOAL_HAS_A_PROB.roster_consequence: If the answer is 'sell to economy', the roster is missing its comparators entirely — lounge aggregators are absent from all four tiers. Flagged for the roster audit alongside F-45.

finding_F55_FOURTH_AI_ASSISTANT.claim: Iberia ships a chat assistant, 'Ibot', present on this page.
finding_F55_FOURTH_AI_ASSISTANT.running_count: Fourth competitor with a conversational assistant: Booking.com (trip planner / message composer), Expedia (Romie, though absent from its homepage), Kayak (IA, prominent in the header), Iberia (Ibot). Assistant commoditisation is now observed first-hand on four of five products captured.

accessibility_note.observation: Iberia's main navigation carries three dedicated accessibility destinations: /es/accesibilidad/vuelo-con-accesibilidad/, /es/accesibilidad/reservar-asistencia-vuelo/ (how to book assistance) and /es/es/perros-de-asistencia/ (assistance dogs).
accessibility_note.comparison: Booking.com publishes one accessibility statement that names no standard (F-06). Iberia routes accessibility as an operational service with a booking path, not as a compliance document.
accessibility_note.note: Accessibility was descoped from competitor analysis by the client. Recorded as an incidental observation only; not pursued.
